ROLE: Borrow the stored client identifier and report its length, so same-identifier takeover can compare two sessions without copying.

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: owner of the identifier copy and its length

LOGIC.INPUT: s: borrowed session pointer, possibly NULL. out_len: optional output slot for the length in bytes.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If out_len is not NULL write 0 into it first, so every return path leaves it defined. 2) If s is NULL return NULL. 3) If s->client_id is NULL (no CONNECT accepted yet, or a failed identifier store) return NULL with *out_len already 0. 4) Otherwise write s->client_id_len into *out_len and return s->client_id. The identifier bytes are owned by the session and are NOT NUL terminated, so a caller must compare id_len bytes explicitly; the returned pointer stays valid until the next session_set_client_id(), session_close_immediately() or session_destroy() on the same session.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: Borrowed pointer to the stored identifier bytes plus its byte length, or NULL with *out_len == 0 when no identifier is stored or s is NULL.
INVARIANTS_USED: the client identifier is a length-delimited byte string, never a C string
a stored identifier is owned by exactly one session and released by the same session
the identifier pointer is invalidated only by a mutating call on that session
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is NULL or points to a live session; out_len is NULL or points to a writable size_t.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: *out_len is 0 or the stored identifier length; the session is otherwise unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe with respect to session_set_client_id() on the same session.
